statement (modern): A surface with p_g=0 and q>0 has an irrational pencil whose base has genus q.
repair and reference: Chapter IX §§4,11; Albanese factorization; commentary cp2-x-1.
notes: Enriques writes p_a=−q and calls an elliptic-base fibration a fascio ellittico.

statement (modern): A moving integral linear system with C²>2p_a(C)−2 forces birational ruledness; regular ruled surfaces are rational.
gap or error (if any): Announced here; proof is given in §2 with gaps in the classical family argument.
repair and reference: Minimal-model nefness of K for nonruled surfaces; cp2-x-2.
notes: Announcement retained separately from its later proof.

statement (modern): If p_g=0 and p_a<−1, the surface is birationally ruled over a curve of genus −p_a.
repair and reference: Proved in §4; cp2-x-4.
notes: Announcement.

statement (modern): For p_g=0 and p_a=−1, the Albanese fibration has rational fibres (the ruled case) or fibres of genus at least one.
repair and reference: Chapter IX pencil theorem; cp2-x-1.
notes: The two cases separate fibre genus from base genus.

statement (modern): Every nonruled p_g=0, q=1 surface has a second rational-base pencil of mutually isomorphic elliptic curves.
gap or error (if any): False in general when the Albanese fibre has genus one; nontranslation monodromy is omitted.
repair and reference: Free product quotient with no vector field; cp2-x-11; valid if the Albanese fibre genus exceeds one, cp2-x-10.
notes: This overstatement announces §§10–13.

statement (modern): Every nonruled p_g=0, q=1 surface admits a one-dimensional elliptic group of birational automorphisms.
gap or error (if any): False without the translation-monodromy hypothesis.
repair and reference: Restrict to the translation class; cp2-x-11 and cp2-x-12.
notes: Must not be used to prove the ruledness criterion for the omitted family.

statement (modern): For n=C² and π=p_a(C), (C+jK_X)·C=n+j(2π−2−n), giving 2π−2, 4π−4−n, 6π−6−2n for j=1,2,3.
gap or error (if any): Requires arithmetic genus and adjoint classes on a smooth model.
repair and reference: Adjunction; cp2-x-2.
notes: Each displayed term is the specialization of the stated general formula.

statement (modern): If n>2π−2 for a nef moving integral C, the sequence of effective successive adjoints terminates.
gap or error (if any): Fixed components and base resolution must be handled in the adjoint interpretation.
repair and reference: An effective divisor has nonnegative intersection with nef C; cp2-x-2.
notes: The same calculation gives P_m=0 for every m>0.

statement (modern): A regular surface with p_g=p_a=P_2=0 is rational.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo rationality criterion; Part 1 and cp2-x-2.
notes: The printed footnote points to Cap. V §4.

statement (modern): A surface fibred in rational curves over a curve of genus p is birationally ruled of genus p.
gap or error (if any): Over the complex numbers; the function-field conic is split.
repair and reference: Tsen's theorem and the rational-fibration criterion; cp2-x-2.
notes: Enriques–Conforto citation supplied by the source.

statement (modern): For a base of genus p>1, the twists C+pH−pH̄ produce a p-dimensional family of distinct linear-equivalence classes restricting equivalently to a fibre H.
gap or error (if any): Effectivity and the required dimensions are not established merely by writing the twists.
repair and reference: Control Picard twists and restriction; the minimal-model proof avoids this step; cp2-x-2.
notes: Here H is Enriques's fibre K, not the canonical class.

statement (modern): The preceding twisting argument implies s=C·H>1.
gap or error (if any): The stated argument alone does not prove this implication; effectivity and component control are missing.
repair and reference: Use the complete negative-canonical-intersection proof; cp2-x-2.
notes: Not accepted as an independent general lemma about all horizontal curves.

statement (modern): If the smooth general fibre H has genus ρ, then (C+jK_X)·H=s+j(2ρ−2).
repair and reference: Adjunction and H²=0; cp2-x-2.
notes: Explains why the last adjoint is claimed to have horizontal degree m≥2.

statement (modern): A degree-m map of a smooth curve to a genus-p curve satisfies g≥m(p−1)+1.
gap or error (if any): Characteristic zero; ramification is nonnegative.
repair and reference: Riemann–Hurwitz; cp2-x-2.
notes: For p>1 and m≥2, this exceeds p.

statement (modern): An integral terminal adjoint of genus greater than q must have a further positive-dimensional adjoint.
gap or error (if any): Uses adjoint Riemann–Roch and the relevant nonspeciality/effectivity conditions.
repair and reference: The numerical obstruction is valid with these hypotheses; cp2-x-2.
notes: This is the contradiction intended for the p>1 case.

statement (modern): A reducible terminal adjoint has at least one component meeting H in at least two points.
gap or error (if any): Not implied just by the existence of twists by H−H̄; components could each be sections unless additional conditions are proved.
repair and reference: Replace the incomplete component argument by minimal-model nefness; cp2-x-2.
notes: A substantive gap in the classical proof, not a transcription error.

statement (modern): In the p=1 terminal case the adjoints form an elliptic family of elliptic curves of positive self-intersection ν.
gap or error (if any): Requires existence and dimension control of the family; the exclusion of an independent irrational pencil comes from p_g=0.
repair and reference: Chapter IX and cp2-x-2.
notes: The source abbreviates several steps.

statement (modern): For an elliptic family whose members meet once, equivalent pairs are parametrized by a rational g¹₂ and their intersections yield rational curves on the surface.
gap or error (if any): The complete g¹₂ is rational, but the incidence construction and its sweeping property are not proved.
repair and reference: Distinguish a complete g¹₂ from the full symmetric square; cp2-x-2.
notes: Lüroth is invoked in the source.

statement (modern): Imposing ν−1 points on a ν-dimensional elliptic-family system reduces the self-intersection to one.
gap or error (if any): Independence of conditions, irreducibility and existence of the resulting family need justification.
repair and reference: The modern ruledness proof does not depend on this reduction; cp2-x-2.
notes: Source treats ν>1 by reduction to ν=1.

statement (modern): A surface containing an integral linear system of dimension at least two with n>2π−2 is birationally ruled.
gap or error (if any): The conclusion is correct; the printed continuous-family proof is incomplete.
repair and reference: For nonruled X, write K_X=μ* K_Y+E with K_Y nef; a moving C has K_X·C≥0; cp2-x-negative-canonical.

statement (modern): Only surfaces birationally ruled can have infinitely many exceptional curves, and a nonruled surface has a model without exceptional curves.
gap or error (if any): Do not read this as saying every ruled model has infinitely many irreducible (−1)-curves; P² has none.
repair and reference: A nonruled surface's (−1)-curves lie in its finite exceptional locus over the minimal model; cp2-x-2.
notes: Historical terminology for exceptional curves requires care.

statement (modern): The quantity a(C)=C²−2p_a(C)+2=−K_X·C is additive in divisor classes.
gap or error (if any): Arithmetic genus is essential.
repair and reference: Adjunction; cp2-x-2.
notes: Allows reduction of an effective divisor to an integral component.

statement (modern): If an integral nonexceptional curve C satisfies C²>2p_a(C)−2, then X is birationally ruled.
gap or error (if any): Correct for an integral curve excluding a (−1)-curve; false with geometric genus substituted for arithmetic genus.
repair and reference: Minimal-model proof in cp2-x-negative-canonical.
notes: Single-curve extension attributed to Campedelli.

statement (modern): For n=C² and π=p_a(C), p_a(sC)=sπ+s(s−1)n/2−s+1.
repair and reference: Adjunction for sC; cp2-x-2.
notes: Valid for nonreduced divisors as arithmetic genus.

statement (modern): The self-intersection of sC is n_s=s²n.
repair and reference: Bilinearity of intersection; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): For sufficiently large s, dim|sC|≥p_a(X)+n_s−p_a(sC)+1>0 in the positive-square case.
gap or error (if any): Requires h²(O_X(sC))=0; Riemann–Roch alone does not give irreducibility or absence of fixed components.
repair and reference: Ample intersection excludes K_X−sC for large s; cp2-x-2.
notes: The source's assertion that the whole system is irreducible is stronger than the displayed estimate.

repair and reference: Substitution into the previous two formulas; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): For a rational integral C satisfying n>−2 and not a (−1)-curve, n≥0.

repair and reference: Adjunction and integrality; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): A smooth rational curve with C²=0 moves in a rational pencil and makes the surface birationally ruled.
gap or error (if any): The deformation/linear-system argument is suppressed.
repair and reference: Normal bundle O_P¹ and rational-fibration criterion; cp2-x-2.
notes: The source argues using a sufficiently large multiple |sC|.

statement (modern): For a terminal adjoint on p_g=0, its arithmetic genus π is at most q=−p_a.
gap or error (if any): Requires the precise terminal-adjoint hypotheses and the earlier adjoint dimension theorem.
repair and reference: Retain only in the historical argument's setting; cp2-x-2.
notes: Not a general genus bound on curves of the surface.

statement (modern): For a pencil cut from the terminal system, δ−n−4π=−12q−ṗ⁽¹⁾+9.
gap or error (if any): The dotted linear genus is model-dependent.
repair and reference: Noether and Zeuthen–Segre formulas; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): Riemann–Roch gives r≥n−π+1−q for the terminal system.

repair and reference: Surface Riemann–Roch; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): The two preceding formulas imply 5π+r≥11q+ṗ⁽¹⁾−8+δ≥11q+ṗ⁽¹⁾−8.

repair and reference: Retain the terminal-adjoint and p_g=0 setting; use cp2-x-negative-canonical for a complete proof.

statement (modern): A complete degree-two linear series on an elliptic curve is parametrized by P¹.
gap or error (if any): Do not confuse that linear series with the entire symmetric square.
repair and reference: Riemann–Roch on an elliptic curve; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): If adjunction terminates in the stated surface-theoretic setting, the surface belongs to the ruled family.
gap or error (if any): A summary of the preceding theorem, whose printed proof is a sketch.
repair and reference: Minimal-model nefness/nonvanishing; cp2-x-2.
notes: The starting positive moving system is part of the adjunction context.

statement (modern): A minimal nonruled complex surface has absolute linear genus p⁽¹⁾=K²+1≥1.
gap or error (if any): Needs the minimal model: blowing up lowers K².
repair and reference: K nef and K²≥0; Part 1, Chapter VI §1; cp2-x-2.

statement (modern): For a base-point-free positive-genus fibration on a minimal nonruled surface, each singular fibre has nonnegative local Zeuthen–Segre contribution.
gap or error (if any): The printed treatment of arbitrary singular components is abbreviated.
repair and reference: δ(F)=K_X·(F−F_red)−F_red²+Σμ_x(F_red)≥0; cp2-x-defect.

statement (modern): If the total singular-fibre contribution is zero, every degenerate fibre is a multiple of a smooth elliptic curve.

repair and reference: Equality in cp2-x-defect; cp2-x-3.

statement (modern): Write a fibre F=Σt_iθ_i and s_hk=θ_h·θ_k for its component multiplicities and intersection numbers.

gap or error (if any): For singular components use arithmetic genera with local corrections, or normalization genera with the full singularity terms.

statement (modern): For a minimal nonruled surface, θ_i²≤2p_a(θ_i)−2.
gap or error (if any): The same inequality with geometric genus may fail for singular θ_i without correction.
repair and reference: Adjunction and nefness of K_X; cp2-x-3.
notes: This is the positivity input behind the component estimate.

statement (modern): For F=tθ with θ smooth of genus ρ and θ²=0, δ(F)=(t−1)(2ρ−2).
gap or error (if any): The footnote prints t+1 in place of t−1.
repair and reference: Direct Euler characteristic/adjunction calculation; cp2-x-3.

statement (modern): The component estimate implies δ(F)≥F_red·(F−F_red), after dropping the nonnegative off-diagonal intersection sum.
gap or error (if any): Singularity conventions must match those of the preceding formula.
repair and reference: Expand the intersection product; cp2-x-3.
notes: F_red is denoted C* in the source.

statement (modern): For a fibre F and D=F_red, D·F=0, so D·(F−D)=−D².
repair and reference: Every fibre component is orthogonal to the fibre class; cp2-x-3.
notes: Core reduction of Franchetta's argument.

statement (modern): A vertical effective reduced divisor D cannot have D²>0.
gap or error (if any): The growth proof suppresses the eventual vanishing of h²(O_X(rD)).
repair and reference: Hodge index gives the negative semidefinite intersection form on fibre components; cp2-x-3.

statement (modern): If D²=i>0 and p_a(D)=ρ, then dim|rD|≥p_a(X)+r²i/2−r(2ρ−2−i)/2 for large r.
gap or error (if any): The print has two errors: −r should be +r in the left expansion, and the trailing +1 on both sides belongs to the h⁰ bound, not the projective dimension.
repair and reference: Surface Riemann–Roch with h²=0; cp2-x-3.
notes: Source line 262; both printed defects confirmed visually. Only the quadratic leading term is needed.

statement (modern): For a connected fibration over a genus-p base, dim|rF|=r−p for sufficiently large r.
gap or error (if any): Uses connected fibres and a fibre over a point; Riemann–Roch on the base.
repair and reference: f_*O_X=O_B and projection formula; cp2-x-3.
notes: Provides the linear growth in the contradiction.

statement (modern): Because F−F_red is effective, h⁰(rF_red)≤h⁰(rF), contradicting quadratic growth if F_red²>0.
repair and reference: Multiplication by the section of r(F−F_red); cp2-x-3.
notes: The print's 'è quindi' is a grammatical misprint for 'e quindi'.

statement (modern): In the degenerate-fibre equality case, the reduced support is a single component of square zero and genus one.
gap or error (if any): The case t=1 must be separated: a reduced smooth higher-genus fibre has δ=0 too.
repair and reference: Use the equality analysis of cp2-x-defect for a genuinely degenerate fibre.
notes: The source's final conclusion is valid in the stated degenerate-fibre scope.

statement (modern): If p_g=0 and q>1, the Albanese fibre must be rational, so the surface is ruled of base genus q.
gap or error (if any): Relies on the earlier pencil theorem and the nonnegative local-contribution lemma.
repair and reference: e(X)=12(1−q)−K²<0 contradicts e(X)=4(q−1)(g−1)+Σδ≥0 for g≥1; cp2-x-4.
notes: Main theorem of §4.

statement (modern): For the genus-q base and genus-π fibre, Δ−4+4(q−1)(π−1)=12p_a−p⁽¹⁾+9.
gap or error (if any): p⁽¹⁾ is absolute on the minimal model.
repair and reference: Noether and Zeuthen–Segre; cp2-x-4.
notes: With p_a=−q this yields the displayed contradiction.

statement (modern): If π≥1 and q>1, Δ≤13−12q−p⁽¹⁾<0, contradicting Δ≥0.
repair and reference: Use p⁽¹⁾≥1 and q≥2; cp2-x-4.
notes: Equivalent to the Euler-characteristic proof in the commentary.

statement (modern): For a minimal nonruled p_g=0, q=1 surface fibred over an elliptic curve, K²=0 and the total fibre defect Δ=0.
gap or error (if any): Uses nefness of K and the local contribution lemma.
repair and reference: 0=12χ=K²+e and e=Σδ; cp2-x-5.
notes: The source writes I=Δ−4=−12−p⁽¹⁾+9, hence p⁽¹⁾=1 and Δ=0.

statement (modern): In the genus-π>1 Albanese case, Δ=0 implies that every fibre is smooth, reduced and irreducible.
gap or error (if any): A multiple F=mD with smooth reduced D contributes (m−1)(2g(D)−2), not (m−1)(2π−2) when π denotes the general-fibre genus.
repair and reference: Equality case of cp2-x-defect and 2π−2=m(2g(D)−2); cp2-x-5.
notes: A nonreduced elliptic fibre would force π=1, excluded here.

statement (modern): Lemma I: there is an effective parabicanonical divisor restricting to |2K_H| on every fibre H and formed of disjoint elliptic components.
gap or error (if any): The limiting-member argument does not establish that a member acquires a whole fibre; genus one alone does not establish the component structure.
repair and reference: Isotrivial product quotient, character eigensections and nefness/adjunction; cp2-x-5 and cp2-x-10.
notes: The divisor may be nonreduced or disconnected.

statement (modern): For every i>2 there is an effective para-i-canonical divisor with the same disjoint elliptic-component property.
gap or error (if any): The same incidence/effectivity gap as for Lemma I persists.
repair and reference: Choose an eigensection of H⁰(H,iK_H) and twist by its character on the elliptic base; cp2-x-5.
notes: The corresponding untwisted P_i need not be positive.

statement (modern): The complete bicanonical series on a genus-π>1 fibre has degree 4π−4 and projective dimension 3π−4.
repair and reference: Curve Riemann–Roch and h¹(2K_H)=0; cp2-x-5.
notes: Enriques writes g^{3π−4}_{4π−4}.

statement (modern): The first adjoint H+K_X has arithmetic genus 3π−2 when K_X²=0 and H²=0.
repair and reference: Adjunction; cp2-x-5.
notes: The print refers to H′, not H″; this displayed genus is correct.

statement (modern): The second adjoint |H+2K_X| has dimension at least 3π−4.
gap or error (if any): Use h²=0; equality is not automatic from the numerical characters.
repair and reference: Intersect K_X−(H+2K_X) with nef H to exclude effectivity; Riemann–Roch; cp2-x-5.
notes: The source expresses the lower bound through the first-adjoint genus.

statement (modern): If the restriction of H⁰(H+2K_X) to the fibre is not injective, there is an effective bicanonical divisor.
gap or error (if any): The source phrases the sufficient condition as incompleteness of the induced series; dimension comparison then supplies the kernel.
repair and reference: Exact sequence for restriction to H; cp2-x-5.
notes: Kernel H⁰(2K_X) gives the required residual divisor.

statement (modern): An effective divisor linearly or algebraically equivalent to 2K_X has square zero and arithmetic genus one.
gap or error (if any): The component conclusion additionally needs nefness and absence of rational curves.
notes: Printed as 3p⁽¹⁾−2=1.

statement (modern): Twisting H+2K_X by differences of fibres produces an elliptic family whose members have the same bicanonical restrictions.
gap or error (if any): Effectivity for each twist follows from the same Riemann–Roch bound; the total projective family requires a Picard-family construction.
repair and reference: Projection/restriction and Riemann–Roch; cp2-x-5.
notes: An algebraic-equivalence family is distinct from a single linear system.

statement (modern): A positive-dimensional family through a fixed bicanonical fibre-divisor must contain a member with that whole fibre as a component.
gap or error (if any): The conclusion does not follow from the dimension count alone; proper incidence and boundary intersection need proof.
repair and reference: Use the product-quotient existence argument instead; cp2-x-5.
notes: This is a proof gap, not a false statement of Lemma I.

statement (modern): For A_i=H+iK_X, the Riemann–Roch lower bound is dim|A_i|≥(2i−1)π−2i for i≥2.
gap or error (if any): The print calls this the dimension of the continuous system; a family of distinct effective Picard twists has one extra parameter.
notes: Separate a numerical lower bound from actual dimension.

statement (modern): Different para-pluricanonical divisors need not have distinct reduced supports.
repair and reference: Coefficients on fixed elliptic components can differ; cp2-x-5 and cp2-x-7.
notes: The source explicitly identifies this obstruction before Lemma II.

statement (modern): A paracanonical divisor restricts to degree 2π−2 on the genus-π fibre.
repair and reference: Adjunction and algebraic-equivalence invariance of intersection; cp2-x-5.
notes: Explains the possible common support of all the constructed multiples.

statement (modern): Lemma II: there exist two elliptic divisors with different reduced supports whose suitable multiples are para-pluricanonical and restrict equivalently to each H.
gap or error (if any): The printed proof has divisor-selection, norm and distinct-support gaps.
repair and reference: A product quotient supplies an elliptic pencil; divisible pluricanonical systems contain divisors on distinct fibres; cp2-x-6 and cp2-x-10.

statement (modern): For a nontrivial η∈Pic⁰(H)[2], L_H=K_H+η satisfies 2L_H∼2K_H and h⁰(L_H)=π−1.
repair and reference: Riemann–Roch and h⁰(−η)=0; cp2-x-6.

statement (modern): A divisor restricting to K_H+η has an adjoint restricting to 2K_H+η, a nonbicanonical half of 4K_H.
repair and reference: Restriction of the canonical class and torsion arithmetic; cp2-x-6.

statement (modern): Hypothesis I requires a rationally varying noncanonical torsion-root series on the fibres.

statement (modern): Hypothesis II requires a rationally varying divisor in the given series.

statement (modern): If two divisors have equivalent restrictions on all smooth irreducible fibres, their difference is vertical and hence pulled back from the base.

statement (modern): In the even-genus case the vertical difference in 2L′−2H″ can be chosen twice a divisor of fibres.

statement (modern): The continuous family of adjusted adjoints has a member H+D, yielding a second elliptic divisor D.

statement (modern): P4=P6=0 characterizes birationally ruled complex surfaces.

statement (modern): Every nonruled complex surface has a nonzero section of some positive pluricanonical bundle.
repair and reference: Classification/Chapter X; κ≥0 for a nonruled smooth projective complex surface.

statement (modern): The four announced classes are ruled, canonical torsion, pluricanonical genus-one fibration, and general type.
gap or error (if any): Announcement here, not an independent proof; absolute p^(1) must refer to a minimal model.

notes: The precise P12 table is stated on pp.456–458.

statement (modern): Ruled surfaces have infinitely many noneliminable exceptional curves (historical wording).
gap or error (if any): False if exceptional is uniformly translated as an irreducible (−1)-curve: P² and P¹×P¹ have none.

notes: Repeated pp.456,463; not a transcription error.

statement (modern): Canonical-torsion surfaces satisfy n=2π−2 for sufficiently positive pure systems on the minimal model.
gap or error (if any): The converse for an arbitrary base-point-free pencil is false.
repair and reference: Adjunction plus Hodge index for ample H and nef K; a genus-one fibre on κ=1 has equality too.
notes: Class B.

statement (modern): Classes C and D have n<2π−2 for sufficiently positive H.
gap or error (if any): Needs KH>0; arbitrary elliptic fibres are exceptions to indiscriminate wording.
repair and reference: Use ample H on a minimal surface with nontrivial nef K.
notes: Class C has K²=0; class D K²>0.

statement (modern): Ruled surfaces possess continuous birational transformation families; quadratic plane transformations can generate families of unbounded dimension.
gap or error (if any): Specific families and dimension growth are not constructed here.
repair and reference: On B×P¹ use PGL2(C(B)); increasing pole degree gives unbounded parameter spaces.
notes: Source cites Enriques (1893) via Enriques–Chisini, Book V, Chapter II §28, vol.III p.200.

statement (modern): For ruled surfaces over a base of genus >1, the connected birational action is not transitive on the surface.
repair and reference: Aut(B) is finite; the connected action is fibrewise.
notes: Does not assert that all discrete birational maps fix the base pointwise.

statement (modern): An effective rational one-dimensional birational group forces ruledness.
gap or error (if any): Imports the Noether–Enriques ruledness theorem.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. General orbit closures are rational curves.
notes: Criterion 1; source cites Conforto, Book II, Chapter I §§4–6, pp.245,260,262.

statement (modern): A connected group preserving a positive-dimensional linear system and acting nontrivially on its members forces ruledness.
gap or error (if any): Reduction from arbitrary systems to a pencil is incomplete on p.432.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. On a nonruled minimal model Aut⁰ is proper and has trivial homomorphism to PGL.
notes: Criterion 2; the source footnote defines transitively as permuting members in infinitely many ways.

statement (modern): An effective connected group of dimension ≥2 with one-dimensional general orbits, or dimension ≥3 with two-dimensional general orbits, forces ruledness.
gap or error (if any): Point-condition and stabilizer arguments require more than their dimension count.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. An effective abelian-variety action has finite stabilizers; its dimension equals orbit dimension.
notes: Criterion 3; original argument pp.432–433.

statement (modern): A connected family whose iterated products have unbounded dimension forces ruledness.
gap or error (if any): Source wording must mean dimension growth, not merely infinitely many discrete group components.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. On a nonruled minimal model all products through the identity lie in finite-dimensional Aut⁰.
notes: Criterion 4; numerical argument p.433 has an additional curve-stabilizer premise.

statement (modern): The rational trajectories of a one-dimensional rational group give a rational-curve pencil.
repair and reference: Rational quotient; resolve indeterminacy and apply the ruledness theorem.
notes: The capital I in the reference to theorem I) is printed; the punctuation after formano is extraneous.

statement (modern): The group action allows a unisecant directrix of the rational pencil.

repair and reference: Over C(B), Tsen implies a conic has a rational point; a rational ruling is birational to B×P¹.
notes: Attributed to Painlevé before the general Noether–Enriques theorem; original proof not inspected.

statement (modern): A surface invariant under a nontrivial connected projective transformation group is ruled.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. The projective automorphism group is affine.
notes: Source reports Enriques (1893), Fano (1895–1897), via Conforto Book II, Chapter II §37 p.496.

statement (modern): A continuous birational group is contained in an algebraic connected group (Picard observation).

notes: Do not treat bounded-degree pieces of the Cremona group as algebraic groups.

notes: A step in the first part of the source proof, not an additional classification theorem.

repair and reference: Finiteness of Aut(C) for g(C)≥2.
notes: Source calls this Schwarz’s theorem; footnote misprints Schwartz.

statement (modern): A genus-one curve cannot carry an infinite connected group preserving a fixed positive-degree linear series.
repair and reference: The translation stabilizer of a line bundle of degree d>0 is finite; group automorphisms fixing the origin are finite.
notes: The proof uses a projective embedding by a multiple of the series.

statement (modern): In the one-dimensional orbit case, preservation of the induced rational linear series makes the trajectories rational.
gap or error (if any): Needs a nonconstant series of positive degree on the orbit closure.
repair and reference: Apply the preceding genus-zero/genus-one dichotomy and finite line-bundle stabilizer.
notes: Then apply Noether–Enriques ruledness.

statement (modern): The subgroup following this second pencil has rational trajectories because it preserves a positive-degree g¹_n on each trajectory.
gap or error (if any): Conditional on the preceding pencil and subgroup existence.
repair and reference: Finite stabilizer on an elliptic curve excludes elliptic trajectories.
notes: The conditional argument itself is sound.

statement (modern): The centralizer of a projectivity fixes the same fixed points individually and hence preserves a nontrivially acted-on projective line.
gap or error (if any): Not established and false as phrased: commuting transformations may move points within an eigenspace; the required line is not supplied.
repair and reference: Replace by the morphism Aut⁰→PGL and properness of Aut⁰ on the nonruled minimal model; Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2.

repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2.
notes: Criterion 3; source cites Castelnuovo–Enriques, Comptes rendus, 29 July 1895.

statement (modern): A positive-dimensional point stabilizer acts nontrivially on some finite infinitesimal neighbourhood unless it is trivial.
gap or error (if any): Finite-jet detection is plausible but the reduction to an algebraic curve group and invariant pencil needs justification.
repair and reference: An automorphism identical to all orders is the identity; use algebraic-group stabilizers for a complete proof.
notes: Does not validate the prior independent-condition count.

statement (modern): For transforms of a curve with base multiplicities h_i, N_r=n+Σh_i² and Π_r=π+Σh_i(h_i−1)/2.
repair and reference: Blow-up intersection and genus formulas; Part 1 divisor conventions.
notes: Here n and π are those of the resolved moving curve, N_r and Π_r the virtual invariants downstairs.

statement (modern): An r-dimensional family of integral curves has N_r≥r−1 under the characteristic-system assumptions.
gap or error (if any): Requires that the selected orbit family really have dimension r and that the tangent normal-sheaf estimate applies.
repair and reference: For a smooth member, r≤h⁰(N_C/X)≤deg N_C/X+1=N_r+1.
notes: A group parameter dimension alone does not imply equal curve-orbit dimension.

statement (modern): Unbounded r yields Σh_i²>(2π−n)² and Σh_i>2π−n.
gap or error (if any): Conditional on N_r≥r−1 and fixed n,π.
repair and reference: Use Σh_i≥√(Σh_i²); all multiplicities nonnegative.
notes: No sign error in this estimate; it is stronger than required.

statement (modern): N_r−2Π_r=n−2π+Σh_i, hence eventually N_r>2Π_r−2 and ruledness follows.
gap or error (if any): Conditional on the preceding unproved orbit-dimension premise.
repair and reference: Numerical identity is exact; use Chapter X’s criterion, or the automorphism-group repair.
notes: The defect is geometric, not in the blow-up arithmetic.

statement (modern): A nonruled surface with nontrivial maximal connected birational group has either a one-dimensional elliptic group or a transitive two-dimensional group.
gap or error (if any): Uses the preceding ruledness criteria; pass to the minimal model.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2.
notes: This forward classification is valid and must be separated from the later false converse from χ=0.

statement (modern): The one-dimensional group has elliptic orbit curves forming a pencil over a base of genus ρ.
repair and reference: An abelian curve acts with finite stabilizer; the quotient is a curve.
notes: ρ is the base genus, not the fibre genus.

statement (modern): Translating a general divisor and taking equivalence classes of incidence groups constructs a second pencil with elliptic base.
gap or error (if any): Needs the Chapter IX incidence construction and nonconstancy.
repair and reference: Earlier IX-310–IX-333; an isotrivial translation quotient (C×E)/G gives the same second projection.
notes: The two pencils are distinct; source calls their fibres C and K.

statement (modern): For the elliptic-base pencil K, Δ−4=12pa−p^(1)+9.
gap or error (if any): Valid here because the base has genus one; use weighted defects for general singular fibres.
repair and reference: Earlier pp167-236 audit, V-001–V-003 and SUP186-006; Part 1, Chapter V §§1–3.
notes: This is e=Δ=12χ−K², not the formula for an arbitrary higher-genus base.

statement (modern): The connected group permutes all fibres of the second pencil, so Δ=0.
gap or error (if any): Requires that no base point is fixed and all fibres lie in the same orbit, supplied by the elliptic translation action.
repair and reference: A transitive action on the elliptic base makes the fibration smooth after the established model choices.
