gap or error (if any): This single equation alone does not determine the two integers.
repair and reference: Use a finite étale product cover: χ(C×E)=0 and K²=0, then divide by its degree.
notes: Forward group-action hypothesis supplies the additional structure; no false converse is used.

statement (modern): For the elliptic-action case pg equals the genus ρ of the orbit-pencil base.
gap or error (if any): The canonical description must include the differential character; here it is trivial because the action is by translations.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. The Hodge line L is trivial, so pg=h⁰(K_B)=ρ.
notes: This formula is correct under the group hypothesis, false for all χ=0 genus-one fibrations.

statement (modern): The determinant-one example is E×C with g(C)=pg; elliptic covers yield higher determinants.
gap or error (if any): For pg=1 the product has a larger two-dimensional group; the maximal one-dimensional case is then special.
repair and reference: Künneth: q=g(C)+1, pg=g(C), χ=0, K²=0.
notes: Source presents constructions, not a unique normal form.

statement (modern): Elliptic-action families are organized by determinant n, pg, multiple-fibre orders s_i, and transverse-fibre genus π.
gap or error (if any): Integers are constrained by finite group actions and Hurwitz formulas; they do not classify complex structures.
repair and reference: Keep Jacobian, cover and translation data; source itself says only partly independent.
notes: The list interchanges C and K relative to p.434; Campedelli (1935) is cited for genus-two examples.

statement (modern): π=1+n(pg−1)+(n/2)Σ(1−1/s_i) for a transverse fibre of degree n.
gap or error (if any): Assumes exactly the indicated uniform ramification and no additional branch points.
repair and reference: Riemann–Hurwitz: 2π−2=n(2pg−2)+Σn(1−1/s_i).
notes: Here pg is the base genus in the translation case only.

statement (modern): A maximal transitive two-dimensional group on a nonruled surface is abelian and the surface is birational to that group.
gap or error (if any): Source’s curve-translation proof invokes elliptic geometry; properness and stabilizers are implicit.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. A transitive abelian-variety action has finite kernel and quotient an abelian surface.
notes: After replacing the group by its effective quotient, the action is simply transitive.

statement (modern): In the hypothetical noncommutative two-dimensional group, transformations commuting with a chosen one are claimed to form a one-dimensional subgroup, reducing to the elliptic case.
gap or error (if any): The centralizer reduction and the resulting contradiction are sketched; the text does not start from two independently given elliptic subgroups.
repair and reference: On a minimal nonruled surface Aut⁰ is an abelian variety, so a two-dimensional effective connected group is commutative and transitive. Brion (2017), Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §3.
notes: This row records the actual centralizer argument on pp. 435–436. Independent elliptic subgroups, when present, give a product isogeny, not necessarily an isomorphism.

statement (modern): An abelian surface has pg=1, q=2, pa=−1 and p^(1)=1.
gap or error (if any): Uses the earlier characterization of hyperelliptic surfaces and invariant forms.
repair and reference: Translation-invariant cotangent bundle gives K trivial; h⁰(Ω¹)=2; χ=0.
notes: Earlier IX-259–IX-281; source’s hyperelliptic means abelian, not modern bielliptic.

statement (modern): The parameter surface F′ of the commutative group is abelian; a finite stabilizer gives an unramified quotient F′→F.
gap or error (if any): Properness is implicit in the source’s appeal to Chapter IX §9.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. The stabilizer is a finite translation subgroup; an effective commutative transitive action has trivial stabilizer.
notes: Source invokes Lie’s parameter representation, then derives simple transitivity by quotienting the ineffective kernel.

statement (modern): An abelian surface has no effective canonical divisor of positive order on its minimal model.
repair and reference: The unique canonical section is translation invariant and nowhere vanishing; equivalently K_A is trivial.
notes: A positive canonical divisor would be an invariant proper subset, contradicting transitivity.

statement (modern): A positive-dimensional canonical linear system would contradict the ruledness criterion for a nontrivially acted-on linear system.
gap or error (if any): One must verify that the action on the system is nontrivial; invariance of the system alone does not imply it.
repair and reference: Use invariant differential forms to compute pg=1 directly.
notes: The actual canonical-triviality conclusion is correct.

statement (modern): The Jacobian of a genus-p curve has irregularity exactly p.
gap or error (if any): The higher-dimensional restriction version of the third equivalence criterion is asserted, not proved.
repair and reference: h¹(O_J)=dim J=p by invariant (0,1)-forms, or the dual abelian variety; earlier IX-237–IX-250 and IX-268–IX-281.
notes: Source invokes Chapter III §13; the intermediate phrase irregularity≥0 is merely weak, not a contradiction.

statement (modern): Successive special coordinate subvarieties preserve inequivalence of the divisors being counted.
gap or error (if any): Needs injectivity of Pic⁰ restriction for these chosen subvarieties; inequivalent arbitrary divisors need not remain so on arbitrary subvarieties.
repair and reference: Use an actual Pic⁰ restriction theorem, or replace the induction by the invariant-form calculation.
notes: This is the missing premise of the source’s Jacobian irregularity proof.

statement (modern): The symmetric square C^(2) has q=g(C)=p, so families of inequivalent divisors have dimension at most p.
gap or error (if any): Incidence on C is invoked without all injectivity hypotheses.
repair and reference: H⁰(Ω¹_C^(2)) is the diagonal invariant part of H⁰(Ω¹_C×C), of dimension p.
notes: This includes p=1; it does not identify C^(2) with an abelian surface in every genus.

statement (modern): An abelian subvariety V_q inside a Jacobian V_p has irregularity q.
gap or error (if any): Printed ambient/subgroup dimensions are reversed; the lower-bound orbit count needs a sufficiently ample divisor with finite translation stabilizer.
repair and reference: Correct subgroup dimension q in ambient p; use q(V_q)=dim V_q.
notes: Source’s arbitrary V_(q−1) should be chosen sufficiently general/ample.

statement (modern): Poincaré reducibility supplies a complementary abelian subgroup of dimension p−q.
gap or error (if any): The product isogeny generally has a finite kernel and is not an isomorphism.
repair and reference: Milne (2008), Part I, Poincaré reducibility; earlier IX abelian-variety claims.
notes: Source cites Picard–Poincaré interpreted by Castelnuovo, via Enriques–Chisini vol.IV pp.237–241.

statement (modern): An r-dimensional family of divisor classes on V_q yields r+p−q independent classes on V_p, whence r≤q.
gap or error (if any): The asserted sweep construction does not itself verify independent divisor classes or the dimension increment.
repair and reference: Pull back along the product isogeny and use Pic⁰(A×B)=Pic⁰(A)×Pic⁰(B); invariant forms give the dimension directly.
notes: The inequality r+p−q≤p is arithmetically correct once its geometric premise is supplied.

statement (modern): A surface with two-dimensional translation orbit in an abelian variety has pa=−1.
repair and reference: It is an abelian surface up to a finite étale cover/isogeny; χ=0.
notes: For a surface orbit, dimension of the stabilizer is ambient dimension minus two.

statement (modern): Every hyperelliptic surface in the historical sense is birational to such an orbit or a finite unramified cover of one.
gap or error (if any): The printed reference Chapter X §9 is wrong.
repair and reference: Correct reference Chapter IX §9, especially IX-250 and IX-258; finite étale covers of abelian varieties are abelian after choosing an origin.
notes: This characterization presupposes the source’s group/uniformization definition.

statement (modern): For an unramified degree-n cover, pa′+1=n(pa+1); therefore χ remains zero.
gap or error (if any): No branch term is allowed; distinguish an isogeny from a branched cover.
repair and reference: Multiplicativity of χ under finite étale covers; earlier Chapter V §8, SUP186 cover calculations.
notes: Printed Chapter V §28 should be §8; semicolon after V is printed.

statement (modern): The group classification yields elliptic-action surfaces or abelian surfaces, all with pa=−1.
gap or error (if any): Correct forward direction only.
repair and reference: Brion (2017), Some structure theorems for algebraic groups, Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; commentary XI §2. and the translation product-quotient calculation.
notes: The next section attempts the converse and loses the nontrivial Hodge-character case.

statement (modern): An abelian surface has P_m=1 for every positive m.
repair and reference: K_A is trivial, so H⁰(mK_A)=C.
notes: This is the last numerical assertion before §4.

statement (modern): A nonruled surface with pa=−1, pg>1 and K²=0 has an elliptic transformation group.
gap or error (if any): False in the stated pg>1 range: let C→B be a connected étale double cover with g(B)=3 and deck involution σ, and take X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩. Then (pg,q,χ,K²)=(2,3,0,0) and H⁰(T_X)=0. The genus-two-base version has pg=1 and treats the later boundary claim.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Triviality of the Hodge line/differential character is needed for the transformation-group conclusion.
notes: The central converse is false; its numerical premises do imply a genus-one fibration.

statement (modern): When pg>1 and K²=0, the canonical system is composed with genus-one fibres.
gap or error (if any): Interpret on the nonruled minimal model, resolving the canonical map.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §4 and abundance/canonical formula for κ=1.
notes: The source then analyzes restriction of Pic⁰ to a general fibre.

statement (modern): The base genus is either ρ=q=pg+1 or ρ=q−1=pg.
gap or error (if any): The source presents two valid possibilities but subsequently excludes one incorrectly.
repair and reference: Leray: q=ρ+h⁰(L⁻¹); for degree-zero L the last term is one or zero.
notes: This dichotomy locates the missing monodromy exactly.

statement (modern): If the restriction of Pic⁰ to the fibre has positive-dimensional image, a second elliptic-base pencil is obtained.
gap or error (if any): Needs the trace/isotrivial and incidence hypotheses from Chapter IX.
repair and reference: In the translation quotient the second projection to E/G supplies the pencil; earlier IX-310–IX-333.
notes: Correct in the trivial-Hodge-character branch of the argument.

statement (modern): For χ=K²=0 and elliptic fibres, Δ=0.
repair and reference: Earlier pp167-236 audit, V-001–V-003 and SUP186-006; Part 1, Chapter V §§1–3. e(X)=Δ because the smooth fibre has Euler number zero.
notes: This equation is valid for every base genus here.

statement (modern): Δ=0 forces all reduced fibres to be smooth elliptic curves and forces constant j.
gap or error (if any): The full singular-fibre nonnegativity theorem is imported; multiple smooth fibres are allowed.
repair and reference: Chapter X §3; discriminant degree 12χ=0 and extension of j to the complete base.
notes: Constant j does not imply trivial monodromy.

statement (modern): The constant-j fibration admits a transverse pencil of base genus zero or one giving canonical divisors pulled from K_B plus multiple fibres.
gap or error (if any): The construction does not ensure an elliptic base or trivial differential character; the canonical formula omits L.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. The second quotient base can be P¹, while nontrivial L persists.
notes: The error propagates from Chapter X §11.

statement (modern): The constructed transverse pencil is asserted to have fibre genus π strictly greater than the genus ρ of the elliptic-fibration base.
gap or error (if any): The strict comparison is not generally justified. Riemann–Hurwitz gives π≥ρ for ρ≥1, with equality possible. For the determinant-one product B×E, the natural transverse fibres are B and have π=ρ; taking a general B of genus at least two avoids an additional elliptic quotient.
repair and reference: Use π=1+n(ρ−1)+(n/2)Σ(1−1/s_i) with the stated ramification hypotheses, as on p. 435. Replace the unconditional strict sign by the weak inequality and keep the equality case.
notes: New row: the scan on p. 439 has an ordinary strict > with no equality stroke; no transcription error is involved.

statement (modern): The canonical formula yields pg=ρ and excludes ρ=pg+1.
gap or error (if any): False because a nontrivial torsion Hodge line contributes: h⁰(K_B⊗L)=ρ−1.
repair and reference: False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
notes: For B of genus b≥2, the explicit example has pg=b−1 and q=b.

statement (modern): The analogous pg=0, pa=−1 case is elliptic-action or ruled.
gap or error (if any): False as a group classification: the Chapter X V4 quotient has pg=0,q=1,κ=1,Aut⁰=0.
repair and reference: Chapter X §11 counterexample; Catanese et al. (2025), Appendix B and Lemma 1.1.
notes: The cited Chapter X §12 depends on the omitted monodromy case.

statement (modern): For pg=1, pa=−1, K²=0, the canonical divisor has positive order or zero order.
gap or error (if any): Order means the pure divisor on the minimal model, not exceptional divisors after blow-up.
repair and reference: Part 1 minimal-model convention.
notes: An effective positive divisor can be reducible or nonreduced; elliptic canonical curve is historical shorthand.

statement (modern): Positive canonical order in this numerical case implies an elliptic transformation group.
gap or error (if any): False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
repair and reference: Replace by κ=1 and retain both Hodge-character cases.
notes: This is the first of the two asserted families.

statement (modern): Zero canonical order with pg=1,q=2 implies the surface is abelian.
repair and reference: K trivial and q=2 in the smooth projective minimal classification; or the Albanese étale argument when its dimension is two.
notes: The second family is correct.

statement (modern): If q=2 and there is no pencil over a genus-two curve, the Albanese map is generically finite onto an abelian surface.
gap or error (if any): The source uses a Picard-incidence construction requiring restriction/injectivity hypotheses.
repair and reference: If the Albanese image were a curve, its Stein base would have genus q=2; earlier IX-298–IX-332.
notes: This lemma is valid; the false claim is the following exclusion of its exceptional case.

statement (modern): The dual incidence curves L lie on the parameter surface Φ and cannot all be linearly equivalent.
gap or error (if any): Text says on F in the first occurrence; printed slip. Equivalence proof imports the third criterion.
repair and reference: Replace F by Φ; interpret the construction through the Albanese morphism.
notes: Source cites Chapter III §13.

statement (modern): Equivalence of incidence divisors yields equivalence of the associated point groups P(G),P′(G).
gap or error (if any): Conditional on the parameter family and the Severi–Castelnuovo criterion.
repair and reference: Restriction of linear equivalence; a rational family of divisors on a curve maps constantly to Pic.
notes: Source cites Enriques–Chisini Book V, Chapter IV §42 p.483 and Chapter I §10 p.78.

statement (modern): If the L-curves fall into one-dimensional linear-equivalence fibres, F has a pencil whose base has genus two.
gap or error (if any): The original dimension inference must be tied to the Picard/Albanese quotient.
repair and reference: Stein factorization of the Albanese map; pullback identifies the relevant Pic⁰.
notes: The printed L_I′ should be L_P′.

statement (modern): A q=2 surface with pg>0 and a pencil over a genus-two base must satisfy pa≥0 (pg≥2).
gap or error (if any): False; the free involution quotient has q=2,pg=1 and such a smooth genus-one fibration.
repair and reference: False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
notes: It is not a failure of the preceding Albanese lemma.

statement (modern): For that genus-two base, the source writes e=Δ+8(π−1).
gap or error (if any): Coefficient 8 is printed but should be 4.
repair and reference: e=Δ+4(π−1)(2−1); combine with e=12χ−K².
notes: Even with this coefficient repaired the monodromy inference is still false.

statement (modern): For χ=0 over a genus-two base, nefness forces K²=0, Δ=0 and fibre genus π=1.
gap or error (if any): Use the corrected coefficient and nonnegative fibre defects.
repair and reference: Earlier pp167-236 audit, V-001–V-003 and SUP186-006; Part 1, Chapter V §§1–3. 0=K²+Δ+4(π−1).
notes: This numerical conclusion is valid.

statement (modern): The subsequent canonical-divisor description forces pg≥2.
gap or error (if any): False because the Hodge line may be a nontrivial two-torsion line bundle.
repair and reference: False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
notes: The footnote imports Chapter IX §8, whose qualifications must not be discarded.

statement (modern): Every pg=1,pa=−1 surface is generically finite over an abelian surface.
gap or error (if any): False; the preceding counterexample has Albanese dimension one.
repair and reference: False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
notes: This follows in the text from the invalid exclusion of a genus-two base.

statement (modern): For a generically finite morphism a:X→A to an abelian surface, K_X is the ramification divisor.
gap or error (if any): If a has contracted curves, account for them on the chosen smooth model; a literal finite-cover formula applies after the appropriate factorization.
repair and reference: K_X=a* K_A+R=R; ordinary ramification formula.
notes: Does not imply that every pg=1,χ=0 surface has such a morphism.

statement (modern): Elliptic branch components invariant under a connected translation subgroup imply the branched cover admits a lifted elliptic action.
gap or error (if any): Invariance of the reduced branch set alone does not prove invariance of the covering data or a lift.
repair and reference: Check the finite cover/monodromy data; an isogenous acting elliptic group may be required.
notes: Conditional equivariant construction does not recover the omitted Albanese-dimension-one case.

statement (modern): A connected finite étale cover of an abelian surface is abelian after choosing an origin.
repair and reference: Earlier IX-250–IX-258; finite-index sublattice uniformization or the algebraic isogeny theorem.
notes: This branch-free case is valid.

statement (modern): In the translation case over an elliptic base, K_X is Σ(s_i−1)F_i for multiple fibres s_iF_i.
gap or error (if any): Requires trivial Hodge line; the printed fractional expression is numerical shorthand, not a fractional integral divisor.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8.
notes: Keep the reduced fibres F_i in the integral canonical formula.

statement (modern): If there are r≥2 multiple fibres, the bicanonical system has dimension at least r−1.
repair and reference: f_*ω_X² has degree r on the elliptic base; h⁰=r. Residual fixed coefficients are s_i−2.
notes: The display correctly separates a whole fibre from each doubled fractional coefficient.

statement (modern): With one multiple fibre, the fourth canonical system has dimension at least one.
repair and reference: floor(4(1−1/s))≥2 for s≥2; every line bundle of degree≥2 on an elliptic curve has at least two sections.
notes: No need to choose a nonexistent square root of a single reduced fibre.

statement (modern): For pg=1,χ=0, positive canonical order gives P4>1; an abelian surface has P4=1.
gap or error (if any): The proof supplied covers the translation case only; the distinction itself extends to the missing nontranslation case.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula in both cases; κ=0 classification.
notes: Do not infer Aut⁰>0 merely from P4>1.

statement (modern): Nonruled surfaces with a continuous group are characterized by pa=−1 and p^(1)=1.
gap or error (if any): False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1. The converse fails.
repair and reference: Correct forward implication; for κ=1 add trivial action on the elliptic differential.
notes: The final wording also neglects the pg=0 elliptic types already treated.

statement (modern): The summary divides all nonruled surfaces with a continuous group into abelian surfaces with pg=1 and elliptic-action surfaces with pg≥1.
gap or error (if any): The printed pg≥1 restriction omits the bielliptic pg=0,q=1 surfaces already treated in Chapter X; these possess a one-dimensional elliptic automorphism group.
repair and reference: Include the κ=0 bielliptic cases in the forward group classification, separately from properly elliptic translation quotients. Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§3–4.
notes: New row: this omission is distinct from the false converse pa=−1,K²=0 ⇒ continuous group recorded in XI087.

statement (modern): A general abelian surface contains no elliptic subgroup.
repair and reference: A general polarized abelian surface is simple; special nonsimple loci have elliptic factors up to isogeny.
notes: The word general is in moduli, not a claim that no abelian surface has an elliptic curve.

statement (modern): A genus-two Jacobian contains an elliptic curve exactly when the genus-two curve admits an elliptic quotient, with a decomposable compact-type exception.
gap or error (if any): Specify isogeny/dual homomorphism and the product principal-polarization case.
repair and reference: A nonzero homomorphism J(C)→E restricts to a nonconstant C→E; dualize for an elliptic subvariety.
notes: Poincaré reducibility supplies the complementary elliptic factor.

statement (modern): An abelian surface containing an elliptic subgroup has two transverse elliptic fibrations and is isogenous to a product.
gap or error (if any): Product only up to finite isogeny, not generally an isomorphism.
repair and reference: Poincaré reducibility; the two quotient maps have finite joint kernel.
notes: The determinant n counts intersection of the two elliptic subgroups/fibre classes.

statement (modern): For a minimal nonruled surface, pa=−1 implies K²=0.
gap or error (if any): Correct, but the present proof assumes an Albanese surface representation that may not exist, then restricts the branch type.
repair and reference: Use minimal classification and χ>0 for general type; or the corrected Euler argument with the remaining small-pg cases.
notes: A valid numerical conclusion must be separated from the false group characterization.

statement (modern): For ordinary simple branch with normalization genus ρ>1, 24χ(X)≥24nχ(A)+6(ρ−1)−2τ.
gap or error (if any): Requires the hypotheses of Severi’s formula; arbitrary multiple branch components are explicitly left untreated.
repair and reference: Earlier Chapter V §8; χ(A)=0. Modern general covers need full ramification data.
notes: Source footnote 1 acknowledges the missing extension; footnote 2 attributes inequality to base points of the correspondence.

statement (modern): The characteristic-series estimate gives 2δ+3τ≤2(ρ+δ+τ−1).
gap or error (if any): Requires the indicated moving nodal-cuspidal curve family and its characteristic series.
repair and reference: Under these hypotheses, subtract 2δ+2τ to obtain τ≤2(ρ−1).
notes: Do not reject the following arithmetic merely because the general branch case is missing.

statement (modern): τ≤2(ρ−1) and ρ>1 imply 24χ(X)>0, hence pa≥0.
repair and reference: 6(ρ−1)−2τ≥2(ρ−1)>0; χ is integral.
notes: A complete numerical deduction conditional on the preceding geometric assumptions.

statement (modern): For irregular nonruled surfaces I+4=e=13+12pa−p^(1)≥0.
gap or error (if any): Source attributes this to a private communication of Castelnuovo, not a proof here.
repair and reference: Earlier pp167-236 audit, V-001–V-003 and SUP186-006; Part 1, Chapter V §§1–3. Minimal classification or fibration positivity gives nonnegative e in the relevant cases.
notes: The identity itself is Noether’s formula; the inequality is the imported content.

statement (modern): If pg=1 and pa=−1, then p^(1)=1; if also P4=1, the surface is abelian.
gap or error (if any): Correct final numerical/abelian assertions despite the incomplete local proof.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. κ=0 and κ=1 classification, retaining both monodromy cases.
notes: Does not restore the group claim for P4>1.

statement (modern): Two independent holomorphic one-forms, one holomorphic two-form, and trivial pure canonical divisor characterize the abelian case in this setting.
gap or error (if any): The canonical-divisor condition cannot be omitted; independent forms must give a nonzero wedge in the abelian argument.
repair and reference: K trivial, q=2; Albanese/κ=0 classification.
notes: Historical Picard criterion; source cites Picard (1889), Chapter III, and Picard–Simart (1906), vol.II.

statement (modern): Trivial canonical divisor gives local invertibility of the two integrals and four-period abelian uniformization.
gap or error (if any): Requires their wedge to be the nonvanishing canonical form; absence of a divisor alone does not manufacture independent periods.
repair and reference: Holomorphic cotangent trivialization and Albanese covering; period lattice has rank four.
notes: The source explicitly reports Picard’s earlier mistaken belief that the third condition was redundant.

statement (modern): Elliptic-action surfaces have a parametrization elliptic in one parameter and algebraic in the other.
gap or error (if any): This concerns surfaces already possessing the group, not all χ=0 genus-one fibrations.
repair and reference: Translation product-quotient description.
notes: Source cites Painlevé (1895), p.270, and Enriques (1905); original analytic proofs not independently read.

statement (modern): Surfaces with pg=1 and K²=0 fall into K3, abelian, and genus-one-fibration families.
gap or error (if any): The families overlap and the stated rational-or-elliptic base omits genus two in the nontranslation χ=0 case.
repair and reference: Separate κ=0 (K3 or abelian) from κ=1; allow base genera 0,1,2.
notes: The source itself acknowledges some overlap through special moduli.

statement (modern): Regular pg=1,P2=1 surfaces are K3, with polarized families of dimension 19 and suitable models of degree 2π−2 in P^π.
gap or error (if any): Low-genus systems may be multiple maps; nineteen is polarized moduli dimension.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §2, claims VII-116 onward; precise base-point and polarization qualifications there.
notes: No repeated proof is claimed in XI.

statement (modern): Abelian surfaces have suitable canonical-section models of degree 2π−2 in P^(π−2), depending on three moduli.
gap or error (if any): Requires an ample complete system; embedding demands a suitable polarization.
repair and reference: Riemann–Roch: h⁰(L)=L²/2=π−1; polarized abelian moduli dimension three.
notes: Does not apply to every small polarization.

statement (modern): Any smooth projective complex surface with pg=1 satisfies pa≥−1, hence q≤2.
gap or error (if any): The ambient-Picard dimension argument is incomplete.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis plus the Plücker dimension argument; Mendes Lopes & Pardini (2011), Theorem 2.1.1 and §3; commentary XI §8. If q>2, a higher-genus-base fibration contradicts 12χ=K²+e≥0 on the minimal nonruled model.
notes: Proposition a; pa can be 1,0,−1.

statement (modern): For regular pg=1,K²=0, P2>1 and positive canonical order give a rational-base genus-one fibration.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §4 and canonical bundle formula with χ=2.
notes: Proposition b; imported result, not newly proved here.

statement (modern): A pg=1 surface with canonical divisor of order zero has pa=1 or −1.
repair and reference: K3/abelian classification; earlier IX-221–IX-226.
notes: First part of proposition c.

statement (modern): The same zero-canonical-order condition permits P4>1 and an elliptic alternative.
gap or error (if any): Internally inconsistent: K trivial implies every P_m=1. The positive-order alternative has been attached to a zero-order premise.
repair and reference: Separate the two canonical-order cases; scan confirms wording, but does not select a unique emendation.
notes: Additional source slip not already marked by the transcription apparatus.

statement (modern): For pg=q=1 and K²=0, paracanonical curves form an elliptic-base genus-one fibration and P2>1.
gap or error (if any): Virtual adjoint dimensions require a sufficiently positive auxiliary curve; the source does not state that requirement.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. χ=1, deg L=1, base genus one; deg f_*ω²≥2.
notes: Proposition d.

statement (modern): Without an irrational pencil, a surface can be represented generically finitely inside its q-dimensional Picard/Albanese variety.
gap or error (if any): A generically finite map need not be birational onto its image; the source’s further reduction uses an incomplete branch argument.
repair and reference: Earlier IX-290–IX-294; use Albanese dimension two, not an unqualified embedding.
notes: Source cites Chapter IX §11.

statement (modern): For q=3, the translated surface has a two-dimensional characteristic linear system of canonical curves, giving pg≥3.
gap or error (if any): Needs smoothness, an actual divisor embedding, and rank of the characteristic restriction map.
repair and reference: The conclusion follows from the wedge-map inequality without those incidence assumptions.
notes: Not a proof for an arbitrary generically finite Albanese map.

statement (modern): For q>3, sweeping surfaces gives V_(q−1), with a characteristic system of dimension r+q−1 and genus P≥r+q.
gap or error (if any): Existence, smoothness, arbitrary positivity, and independent deformations of the chosen intermediate variety are assumed.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis plus the Plücker dimension argument; Mendes Lopes & Pardini (2011), Theorem 2.1.1 and §3; commentary XI §8.
notes: The letter P here is a higher-dimensional geometric genus, not a surface plurigenus.

statement (modern): The incidence count r+2q−3−x=q gives x=r+q−3.
gap or error (if any): Arithmetic is conditional on unproved equidimensional incidence dimensions.
repair and reference: Separate the dimension equation from the geometric premise; use the wedge proof for the final bound.
notes: The displayed algebra has no arithmetic error.

statement (modern): Restricting the characteristic system leaves dimension r+q−1−(x−1)=3, so pg≥4.
gap or error (if any): Restriction rank/kernel dimensions are not established by the preceding parameter count.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis plus the Plücker dimension argument; Mendes Lopes & Pardini (2011), Theorem 2.1.1 and §3; commentary XI §8. The modern bound pg≥2q−3 is stronger when q≥4.
notes: Do not infer a system’s restriction rank from parameter dimensions alone.

statement (modern): If pg<3 and q>2, an irrational pencil must exist.
gap or error (if any): The local proof is incomplete, but the result is correct.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis plus the Plücker dimension argument; Mendes Lopes & Pardini (2011), Theorem 2.1.1 and §3; commentary XI §8.
notes: In fact the base genus can be taken at least two.

statement (modern): The source’s Euler inequalities are Δ−4≥12pa−p^(1)+9 and 12(pa+1)−p^(1)≤0.
gap or error (if any): Wrong first comparison; second has wrong sign and missing +1. Equality case also prints pa=1 instead of −1.
notes: All errors confirmed in the scan; changing ≤ to ≥ alone is insufficient.

statement (modern): The adjoint of a sufficiently positive curve of genus π has dimension π−1 and cuts a canonical subseries of deficiency one.
gap or error (if any): The source says merely an irreducible system; the dimensions need vanishing/completeness hypotheses.
repair and reference: For ample enough C use 0→K_X→K_X+C→K_C→0 and h¹(K_X)=q=1.
notes: This is the starting calculation for proposition d.

statement (modern): Paradjoint variation yields an effective elliptic paracanonical residual curve and an elliptic pencil.
gap or error (if any): Effectivity of a residual divisor is not automatic from virtual dimension; the needed canonical-fibration structure is unstated.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Degree-one twists on the elliptic base supply the moving fibre and fixed multiple-fibre part.
notes: Earlier IX-188–IX-226 controls paracanonical qualifications.

statement (modern): Twice a paracanonical fibre gives a moving system, hence P2≥2.
gap or error (if any): A literal doubled paracanonical class need not equal 2K for every twist; the bundle-degree calculation is the robust argument.
repair and reference: f_*ω² has degree at least two on an elliptic curve; h⁰ equals degree.
notes: The conclusion is true.

statement (modern): The paraelliptic example in Chapter X §11 has pa=0,pg=1,K²=0.
gap or error (if any): Use the corrected branch/contact construction; not the separate incorrectly counted pa=3,pg=4 example.
repair and reference: Chapter X §11 audit.
notes: The source’s invitation to study other K² is a historical programme.

statement (modern): For nonruled complex surfaces P12=1 is equivalent to torsion canonical bundle on the minimal model.
gap or error (if any): Converse requires the effective plurigenus classification, not only an elementary torsion argument.
repair and reference: Chapter X plus canonical formula and general-type Riemann–Roch.
notes: Four κ=0 types are enumerated.

statement (modern): The pg=q=0, P2=1 case is Enriques, represented by the tetrahedral sextic model with the appropriate qualifications.
gap or error (if any): The model construction is not universal in the unqualified smooth-branch form.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §1, preserving all earlier restrictions and counterexamples.
notes: Canonical order two.

statement (modern): The pg=0,q=1,κ=0 case consists of the seven bielliptic types.
gap or error (if any): The final type is printed III_e rather than III_c.
repair and reference: Chapter X §§16–19; canonical orders 2,3,4,6.
notes: This list is not the list of all pg=0,q=1 surfaces.

statement (modern): The pg=1,q=0 and pg=1,q=2 torsion cases are K3 and abelian respectively.
repair and reference: Chapters VII and IX; K trivial and the κ=0 classification.
notes: All plurigenera equal one in these two cases.

statement (modern): Enriques and bielliptic types have moduli dimensions 10 and respectively 2 or 1.
gap or error (if any): Counts concern the indicated deformation types, not an arbitrary singular projective presentation.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §1 and Chapter X §§16–19.
notes: Source contrasts these eight types with infinitely many polarized K3/abelian families.

statement (modern): K3 and abelian surfaces form infinitely many polarized families distinguished by arithmetic polarization data.
gap or error (if any): The integer is not an absolute invariant of the unpolarized surface.
repair and reference: Chapter VII §2; polarization type (d1,d2) for abelian surfaces.
notes: Printed Chapter XII §2 should be Chapter VII §2.

statement (modern): For primitive abelian-surface polarization the period matrix can be normalized with diagonal block (1,1/δ) and symmetric remaining block (g,h;h,g′).
gap or error (if any): Riemann bilinear relations and positive-definite imaginary part are suppressed; arbitrary g,h,g′ do not define a polarized abelian surface.
repair and reference: Milne (2008), Part I, polarizations and analytic uniformization.
notes: Source cites Enriques–Chisini, Book VI, Chapter III §39, vol.IV p.242.

statement (modern): The divisor δ is the primitive polarization type (1,δ) and determines a degree-δ isogeny to a principally polarized surface.
gap or error (if any): Requires an isotropic subgroup of the polarization kernel and a chosen polarization.
repair and reference: A maximal isotropic subgroup has order δ and gives a principal quotient polarization: Milne (2008), Part I, Proposition 13.8, Remark 13.9, and Corollary 13.10. The resulting principally polarized surface is a genus-two Jacobian or a product: Voight (2021), Theorem 43.5.1.
notes: A principally polarized abelian surface can be a product of elliptic curves rather than a smooth genus-two Jacobian.

statement (modern): For a genus-two curve C, C^(2) is birational to J(C), and residual involutions give the Kummer quotient.
gap or error (if any): The Abel map contracts the canonical pencil; it is not an everywhere isomorphism.
repair and reference: Earlier IX-231–IX-234 and IX-283–IX-289; Part 1 Chapter V §8.
notes: Residual involution on Pic²(C) is x↦a−x.

statement (modern): On the abelian Jacobian model, a residual involution has sixteen fixed points and the quotient has sixteen ordinary double points.
gap or error (if any): The fixed-point count applies on the minimal abelian model, not literally to every point of the blown-up symmetric square.
repair and reference: Solve 2x=a on an abelian surface: |A[2]|=2⁴=16; local quotient by −1 is A1.
notes: The quartic Kummer model here comes from a principally polarized genus-two Jacobian; the Abel map C^(2)→J(C) contracts its canonical pencil.

statement (modern): Products of two residual involutions are translations; finite translation subgroups give étale abelian quotients.
repair and reference: (a−(b−x))=x+(a−b); translations have no fixed points unless trivial.
notes: A cyclic group of order δ can be chosen, but arbitrary subgroups do not automatically realize a prescribed polarization type.

statement (modern): The isogenous quotient may also be described as an unramified cover of a Jacobian in the reverse direction.
gap or error (if any): Requires a dual isogeny, not an equality of quotient and cover degrees without polarization data.
repair and reference: An isogeny φ admits an isogeny ψ in the opposite direction with ψφ=[N]; use the finite-index lattice description. Polarization descent is made precise in Milne (2008), Part I, Proposition 13.8, Remark 13.9, and Corollary 13.10; allow the product alternative of Voight (2021), Theorem 43.5.1.
notes: The source suggests enlarging the involution to an order rδ one.

statement (modern): An abelian variety is an abelian subvariety or quotient of a Jacobian up to isogeny.
gap or error (if any): Do not replace up to isogeny by an isomorphism to a same-dimensional Jacobian.
repair and reference: Earlier IX-237–IX-250; complete-intersection curve and Poincaré reducibility.
notes: Source cites Chapter IX §9.

statement (modern): The dimension g(g+1)/2 of polarized abelian moduli exceeds 3g−3 for curves.
gap or error (if any): Strict inequality holds for g≥4, not for all g; it is equal at g=2,3.
repair and reference: Compute (g−2)(g−3)/2; general g≥4 abelian varieties are not Jacobians, even up to countably many isogeny correspondences.
notes: The argument is about general varieties, not every individual abelian variety.

statement (modern): Since abelian surfaces and genus-two curves each have three moduli, every abelian surface is isogenous to a genus-two Jacobian.
gap or error (if any): Equal dimensions do not prove dominance; decomposable principally polarized surfaces require the compact-type case.
repair and reference: Use the polarization-kernel quotient of Milne (2008), Part I, Proposition 13.8, Remark 13.9, and Corollary 13.10, then the Jacobian/product dichotomy of Voight (2021), Theorem 43.5.1. Equal dimensions alone give no dominance theorem.
notes: Source’s conclusion needs the isogeny theorem, not the parameter count.

statement (modern): An ample curve of arithmetic genus π on an abelian surface has dim|L|=π−2.
gap or error (if any): Ample or appropriate nonspeciality assumption is required.
repair and reference: K_A=0, χ(O_A)=0, Kodaira vanishing and Riemann–Roch: h⁰(L)=L²/2=π−1.
notes: A degree-zero or elliptic-fibre line bundle is outside this calculation.

statement (modern): The system contains finitely many curves with π−2 nodes and normalization genus two.
gap or error (if any): Expected dimension zero proves neither existence nor nodality, irreducibility, or finiteness.
repair and reference: An independent Severi-variety existence/transversality theorem is needed; the polarization-isogeny argument avoids this gap.
notes: For example a product principal theta divisor is reducible, illustrating why a dimension count alone is insufficient.

statement (modern): A genus-two curve on the abelian surface has a two-dimensional translation orbit and trivial translation stabilizer.
gap or error (if any): Requires an integral curve of geometric genus two; its existence is the preceding gap.
repair and reference: Any finite stabilizer acts freely on the normalization; 2=|G|(2g′−2) forces |G|=1. Positive-dimensional stabilizer would make the curve elliptic.
notes: This proof applies also to nodal integral curves; no extra counterexample is asserted.

statement (modern): There is a unique involution of the form x↦a−x preserving that genus-two curve.
gap or error (if any): Existence follows after the Abel–Jacobi factorization; uniqueness uses the trivial translation stabilizer.
repair and reference: The hyperelliptic involution induces inversion after a translation; two such involutions differ by a translation.
notes: Source says this remains true despite special automorphisms of the curve.

statement (modern): Incidence of the genus-two translation orbit identifies the surface with J(C) or a finite quotient of it.
gap or error (if any): The family must be algebraic and the induced homomorphism nondegenerate; curve existence is not proved.
repair and reference: The normalization map C→A extends to J(C)→A; image generates A, hence this is an isogeny.
notes: A clean modern repair once an integral genus-two curve exists.

statement (modern): Two abelian integrals with four periods in a larger Jacobian define an abelian-surface factor.
gap or error (if any): Need a rational lattice/polarization sub-Hodge structure, not arbitrary complex linear forms.
repair and reference: Poincaré reducibility and abelian subvarieties; Milne (2008).
notes: Source cites Picard–Poincaré via Castelnuovo, Enriques–Chisini vol.IV p.234.

statement (modern): An elliptic factor of J(C3) corresponds to a nonconstant finite map C3→E.
gap or error (if any): The homomorphism to E must be nonzero; its restriction to the Abel image then cannot be constant.
repair and reference: Universal property of the Jacobian and duality.
notes: Historical unirational transform here means a finite map of curves, not a rational parametrization.

statement (modern): A degree-n map from a genus-three curve to an elliptic curve with simple branching has four branch points.
repair and reference: Riemann–Hurwitz: 2·3−2=n(2·1−2)+4.
notes: The generic simple-branch hypothesis matters.

statement (modern): Four arbitrary branch positions with substitutions construct the required connected cover.
gap or error (if any): Permutations must satisfy the elliptic-base global monodromy relation and generate a transitive action.
repair and reference: Riemann existence theorem with admissible monodromy; source cites Enriques–Chisini Book V, Chapter IV §38 p.427.
notes: Arbitrary permutations without these conditions do not define the claimed cover.

statement (modern): The corresponding Hurwitz family has four moduli: one elliptic modulus plus four branch points modulo translation.
gap or error (if any): For a fixed admissible discrete monodromy type and generic simple branch positions.
repair and reference: 1+4−1=4; finite automorphism identifications do not change dimension.
notes: The count itself is valid under these hypotheses.

statement (modern): Subtracting the elliptic modulus leaves three independent moduli of the complementary abelian surfaces.
gap or error (if any): The Prym-map image dimension and fibre dimension are not established by subtraction.
repair and reference: A separate dominance/generic-fibre theorem is required; do not infer it from total dimension.
notes: The source supplies no such proof.

statement (modern): The intersection-subgroup quotient of J(C3) is the Jacobian of a compact-type genus-three curve with genus-two and elliptic components.
gap or error (if any): Complementary factors give a product up to isogeny; that particular abelian-surface factor is not shown principally polarized.
repair and reference: Poincaré reducibility (Milne, 2008, Part I, Proposition 10.1) gives complementary factors only up to isogeny. A further polarization isogeny (Milne (2008), Part I, Proposition 13.8, Remark 13.9, and Corollary 13.10) reaches a principal surface; Voight (2021), Theorem 43.5.1 then gives a genus-two Jacobian or a product degeneration.
notes: The valid product/isogeny construction is weaker than the asserted exact identification.

statement (modern): Rank r of the hyperelliptic parametrization is the number of representatives of a quotient point in a period domain.
repair and reference: It is the generic degree of the finite quotient map.
notes: Source footnote defines the term explicitly.

statement (modern): Certain irregular nontranslation quotients of special abelian surfaces are the pg=0,q=1,κ=0 bielliptic types.
gap or error (if any): Requires the free product-type group actions classified earlier.
repair and reference: Chapter X §§16–19.
notes: Do not generalize to every arbitrary finite quotient of an abelian surface.

statement (modern): Quotient by inversion has sixteen nodes for any abelian surface; suitable polarized Kummer models have degree 2π−2 in P^π.
gap or error (if any): Projective model degree and dimension require suitable base-point-free polarization; changing it does not change the sixteen two-torsion points.
repair and reference: A[2] and local A1 quotient; Chapter VII K3-model qualifications.
notes: δ=1 gives the usual quartic Kummer model.

statement (modern): Exceptional regular finite quotients of abelian surfaces are generated by finite groups and have been completely classified.
gap or error (if any): No group list or proof here; an arbitrary finite correspondence is not automatically Galois.
repair and reference: Retain as a source-reported dependency on Enriques–Severi and Bagnera–De Franchis (1908); exact original hypotheses unverified.
notes: Scan prints hyperellyptiques and dotta; normalize names/titles only with disclosure.

statement (modern): K3 surfaces also admit finite quotients whose resolutions are K3 or Enriques surfaces.
gap or error (if any): Source supplies no classification or proof and does not distinguish all ramification types.
repair and reference: Symplectic finite quotients and fixed-point-free Enriques involutions give the familiar examples; Chapter VII.
notes: Attributed broadly to Godeaux’s school; no invented precise paper is supplied.

statement (modern): P12=0 characterizes rational or birationally ruled surfaces.
gap or error (if any): An effective index-12 theorem is required, not merely eventual plurigenus growth.
repair and reference: Chapter X’s corrected plurigenus criterion.
notes: Class A; source cites Enriques, February 1914 classification note.

statement (modern): P12=1 characterizes surfaces with torsion canonical class on the minimal model.
repair and reference: Chapter X; κ=0 classification, with canonical orders 1,2,3,4,6.
notes: Class B; distinguish linear torsion from a mere numerical calculation.

statement (modern): P12>1 and p^(1)=1 characterize κ=1 surfaces with a pluricanonical genus-one fibration.
gap or error (if any): Use the absolute linear genus of the minimal model.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8.
notes: Class C; the fibration may have no section.

statement (modern): P12>1 and p^(1)>1 characterize surfaces of general type with a pluricanonical model.
gap or error (if any): A chosen canonical or low pluricanonical system need not be birational.
repair and reference: Bombieri (1973), Main Theorem: 5K supplies the canonical model.
notes: Class D.

statement (modern): The ruled class is characterized also by suitable n>2π−2 systems and rational transformation families.
gap or error (if any): Historical exceptional-curve wording and dimension-growth meaning need the §2 qualifications.
repair and reference: Chapter X §§1–2; XI §2 automorphism-group proof.
notes: Existence of one suitable system, not an inequality for every divisor.

statement (modern): pa=P2=0 characterizes a rational surface.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo rationality; Part 1 Chapter VI §4 and Chapter X.
notes: Within ruled surfaces q=−pa, so pa=0 is the rational case.

statement (modern): An irrational ruled surface of base genus b has pa=−b; pa<−1 alone will characterize b>1.
gap or error (if any): The converse is deferred to §8.
repair and reference: Künneth/birational invariance; corrected CDF–Euler argument in XI §8.
notes: No separate hypothesis pg=0 is ultimately needed.

statement (modern): For pa=−1, P4=P6=P12=0 singles out elliptic ruled surfaces.
repair and reference: Chapter X plurigenus criterion.
notes: The printed extra closing parenthesis is typographical only.

statement (modern): On a minimal κ=0 surface, n=2π−2 for every smooth member of a base-point-free system.
repair and reference: K numerically trivial and adjunction.
notes: The converse from a single nonample system is not asserted by the repair.

statement (modern): For complete ample systems the projective dimensions are π,π−1,π−2 as χ=2,1,0.
gap or error (if any): Very ampleness is extra; low-degree systems may yield multiple maps.
repair and reference: Kodaira vanishing plus RR: dim|H|=π+χ−2.
notes: Source lists pg=pa=1; pg=pa=0; pa=−1.

statement (modern): K3 and abelian surfaces have canonical hyperplane sections in the sense O_H(H)=K_H.
gap or error (if any): For suitable smooth hyperplane sections of the chosen model.
repair and reference: Adjunction and K_X trivial.
notes: Class B′.

statement (modern): For Enriques and bielliptic surfaces, a multiple sH restricts to sK_H, with s∈{2,3,4,6}.
gap or error (if any): The restricted torsion may have smaller order; no exact-order assertion follows automatically.
repair and reference: sK_X is linearly trivial, then adjunction.
notes: Class B″; source calls the section a division of its s-canonical series.

statement (modern): B″ consists of eight deformation types: Enriques plus seven bielliptic types.
gap or error (if any): The source prints B′ in the paragraph assigning the finite eight families.
repair and reference: Correct B′ to B″; Chapters VII and X.
notes: These are families, not eight individual surfaces.

statement (modern): B′ has infinitely many polarized families, of dimensions 19 for K3 and 3 for abelian surfaces.
gap or error (if any): Polarization data do not partition unpolarized surfaces uniquely.
repair and reference: Chapter VII moduli discussion and XI §6.
notes: Infinitely many possible degrees/types, with each moduli space positive dimensional.

statement (modern): Every B″ surface has a genus-one pencil, whereas a general B′ surface need not.
gap or error (if any): The printed first B′ and final B″ in this sentence are interchanged.
repair and reference: Enriques isotropic divisors and bielliptic projections; general K3/abelian surfaces can have no isotropic divisor.
notes: The corrected assertion is true over C.

statement (modern): The determinant is the least degree of a rationally defined effective point group on the generic genus-one fibre.
gap or error (if any): Not the degree of a projective model and not the existence of a section.
repair and reference: Interpret as multisection degree/index of the genus-one curve over C(B).
notes: The separate determinant-one normal forms in Chapter VII do not exhaust all fibrations.

statement (modern): χ, determinant, multiple-fibre data and base genus organize genus-one surfaces into families.
gap or error (if any): These integers do not specify the Jacobian, torsor, monodromy, branch positions or complex structure.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Retain all additional fibration data.
notes: Source presents a classification programme, not an isomorphism classification by integers.

statement (modern): For χ>0 the base genus is ρ=pg−pa=q.
repair and reference: Leray and deg L=χ>0 give h⁰(L⁻¹)=0.
notes: Earlier IX-221–IX-226; Chapter VII irregular extension.

statement (modern): For χ=0 and a second elliptic-base pencil, ρ=pg−pa−1=pg.
gap or error (if any): Correct in the translation/Hodge-trivial case only.
repair and reference: Leray gives q=ρ+1 when L is trivial.
notes: The omitted nontrivial-L case has ρ=q=pg+1.

statement (modern): Plurigenera distinguish all the indicated genus-one families.
gap or error (if any): They detect some numerical data but not all Jacobian, torsor or moduli data.
repair and reference: Canonical-bundle floor formulas; identical plurigenera can occur on nonisomorphic surfaces.
notes: The source cautiously proposes an extension to irregular surfaces rather than proving it.

statement (modern): For fixed pa,pg,K²>0, there are finitely many algebraic families of general-type surfaces.
gap or error (if any): Source gives no uniform pluricanonical exponent or fixed Hilbert polynomial.
repair and reference: Bombieri (1973), Main Theorem; 5K model has polynomial χ+(25t²−5t)K²/2; Hilbert schemes of finite type.
notes: Finitely many irreducible families, not finitely many isomorphism classes.

statement (modern): Canonical or pluricanonical image degree is K² or a corresponding multiple.
gap or error (if any): If the map has degree d or base points, divide the resolved moving self-intersection by d.
repair and reference: For the canonical model embedded by 5K the degree is 25K²; otherwise separate map degree and fixed/base contributions.
notes: Part 1 moving-system convention; Chapter VIII multiple-map examples.

statement (modern): The constructed low-invariant examples suggest regularity for K²=1,2 surfaces.
gap or error (if any): A conjectural observation about the examples is not a theorem; K²=2,pg=q=1 surfaces exist.
repair and reference: Lewis & Lyons (2018), Theorem 2.1: double covers of E^(2), branch |6D0−2G0|. K²=1 regularity follows from Debarre (1982), Theorem 6.1, completed by the 1983 Addendum for the canonical-pencil case.
notes: Source explicitly uses “sembra”; record its conjectural status.

statement (modern): If q≥3, pa≥0 and the canonical system is not composed with a pencil, then p^(1)≥6pa+4.
gap or error (if any): False as printed. The smooth double cover of B_2×E with L of bidegrees (4,3) has (χ,q,K²)=(15,3,72), so 73<88.
repair and reference: Debarre (1982), §1.4; Xiao (1985), §1.3; explicit double-cover calculations in commentary XI §7. A true general irregular bound is K²≥2pg: Debarre (1982), Theorem 6.1, completed by the 1983 Addendum for the canonical-pencil case.
notes: Attributed to Castelnuovo’s private communication, November 1942; scan confirms “not composed with a pencil”.

statement (modern): Under the same canonical-map hypothesis with q=2, p^(1)≥3pa+4.
gap or error (if any): False. The smooth double cover of B_2×P¹ with L=(deg4,O(3)) has (χ,q,pg,K²)=(9,2,10,24), and canonical degree two; 25<28.
repair and reference: Debarre (1982), §1.4; Xiao (1985), §1.3; explicit double-cover calculations in commentary XI §7.
notes: No change of a transcription sign repairs this substantive bound.

statement (modern): Only q=1 with an elliptic-base pencil remains to be examined after those inequalities.
gap or error (if any): Does not follow because the two inequalities are false and higher-q examples occur.
repair and reference: Retain canonical-map degree and Albanese-fibration hypotheses; commentary XI §7 examples.
notes: This is the last sentence of the footnote.

statement (modern): Every surface of general type has pa≥0, equivalently χ≥1.
repair and reference: Standard characteristic-zero general-type positivity, or the corrected negative-χ classification below.
notes: The assertion is true, although the footnote bounds are false.

statement (modern): If there is no irrational pencil, pg>2(q−2), equivalently pg<2pa+4.
gap or error (if any): The local chapter imports an analytic theorem; the source’s weaker no-irrational-pencil hypothesis can be replaced by no base genus≥2 pencil.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis plus the Plücker dimension argument; Mendes Lopes & Pardini (2011), Theorem 2.1.1 and §3; commentary XI §8.
notes: Integer form: pg≥2q−3.

statement (modern): If pg≥2pa+4, there is a pencil over a curve of genus at least two.
repair and reference: Contrapositive of the preceding theorem; pg≥2pa+4 iff pg≤2q−4.
notes: The source says genus>0; the modern theorem gives the stronger ≥2.

statement (modern): pa<−1 implies the existence of such an irrational pencil.
repair and reference: Since pg≥0 and 2pa+4≤0 for integral pa≤−2, apply the contrapositive.
notes: The equality case pa=−2,pg=0 is included.

statement (modern): If pa<−1, the pencil has rational fibres and the surface is ruled over a curve of genus −pa.
gap or error (if any): The displayed Euler equality omits 4(g−1)(b−1) for a general base.
repair and reference: For a nonruled minimal model, K²≥0 and e=Δ+4(g−1)(b−1)≥0 contradict 12χ<0.
notes: The theorem survives the formula correction.

statement (modern): The pg=0 hypothesis in the earlier ruledness criterion is redundant when pa<−1.
repair and reference: Once ruled, pg=0 and q=−pa follow.
notes: Source refers back to Chapter X §4.

statement (modern): For pa=−1 and pg>1, one obtains K²=0.
gap or error (if any): Again the printed Euler formula suppresses the base term; the corrected sum of nonnegative terms suffices.
repair and reference: 0=12χ=K²+Δ+4(g−1)(b−1), with b≥2 and g≥1.
notes: This numerical deduction is valid.

statement (modern): Every pa=−1,pg≠1 surface is elliptic in the transformation-group sense or elliptic ruled.
gap or error (if any): False both for pg>1 and pg=0 because of nontranslation finite monodromy.
repair and reference: For pg>1 use g(B)=3 in X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, where C→B is connected étale of degree two; this gives (pg,q,χ,K²)=(2,3,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. For pg=0 use the Chapter X V4 example. Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §4.
notes: Modern genus-one fibration and historical elliptic group are distinct notions.

statement (modern): For pa=−1,pg=1 the surface is abelian when P4=1 and elliptic-action when P4>1.
gap or error (if any): The abelian branch is correct; the group conclusion in the positive-order branch is false.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Permit κ=1 with either trivial or nontrivial differential character.
notes: Only the reference following “In questo caso” on p. 460 should be Chapter XI §4. The later reference introducing a completion of Chapter X §4 is appropriate and must be retained.

statement (modern): pa=−1 globally characterizes nonruled elliptic-action and abelian surfaces.
gap or error (if any): False: X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩, C→B connected étale double cover, g(B)=2, has (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0) and Aut⁰=0. See cp2-xi-monodromy-example and Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1.
repair and reference: Correct list: abelian, bielliptic, or properly elliptic quasi-bundle of either monodromy type.
notes: The zero-plurigenus equalities in parentheses describe excluded ruled cases; if conjoined as positive hypotheses they need >0 instead.

statement (modern): Within the nonruled χ=0 class, pg=P4=1 characterizes abelian surfaces.
repair and reference: κ=0 table; canonical bundle formula excludes κ=1 at P4=1 in this pg=1 setting.
notes: This useful subcriterion remains true.

statement (modern): Every surface with pa<0 is irrational ruled or elliptic/abelian in the book’s group sense.
gap or error (if any): Incomplete list: properly elliptic χ=0 surfaces with Aut⁰=0 are omitted.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Replace group-elliptic by the full κ=1 quasi-bundle class.
notes: The numerical negative-χ/zero-χ division remains correct.

statement (modern): For nonrational surfaces, pa<0 is equivalent to having a continuous birational transformation group.
gap or error (if any): The implication from pa<0 to existence of a continuous birational group is false; smooth χ=0 nontranslation quotients have no vector fields.
repair and reference: The direction “nonrational surface with a continuous birational group ⇒ pa<0” follows from ruledness or the abelian/elliptic-translation group classification. Brion (2017), Theorem 7.1.1 and Proposition 7.1.4; Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1. The reverse direction is contradicted by X=(C×E)/⟨(σ,[-1])⟩ with g(C/σ)=2, (pg,q,χ,K²)=(1,2,0,0), and H⁰(T_X)=0.
notes: This is the strongest incorrect group-characterization sentence.

statement (modern): pg counts independent holomorphic two-forms and q independent holomorphic one-forms.
gap or error (if any): Equality q=h⁰(Ω¹) uses the smooth projective complex/Hodge setting.
repair and reference: Dolbeault/Hodge symmetry; established conventions in Part 1.
notes: Historical language: double and simple integrals of the first kind.

statement (modern): The wedge of two independent holomorphic one-forms is a holomorphic two-form, possibly zero.
repair and reference: Exterior product Ω¹⊗Ω¹→K_X.
notes: Source attributes the nondependent-integral construction to Noether.

statement (modern): Independent one-forms whose wedge vanishes come from an irrational pencil.
gap or error (if any): The source states the analytic principle without the full construction.
repair and reference: Castelnuovo–de Franchis: the base genus is≥2; explicit closed-form/Stein-factorization proof in commentary XI §8.
notes: Historical citations: De Franchis, Castelnuovo, Enriques, 1905.

statement (modern): The wedge-map geometry yields pg≥2q−3 in the absence of a genus≥2 base pencil.
gap or error (if any): The book omits the dimension argument.
repair and reference: P(ker μ) disjoint from Gr(2,q), dimension 2q−4, forces rank μ≥2q−3.
notes: Modern proof supplied; historical desire for an algebraic proof is not a present open problem.

statement (modern): Every irregular double plane has an irrational pencil (De Franchis result quoted in a footnote).
gap or error (if any): No branch/model hypotheses or proof are supplied in this chapter.
repair and reference: Apply only under the hypotheses of the double-plane theorem; retain as reported historical dependency and use Part 1/Chapter VIII branch analysis.
notes: Do not generalize to arbitrary singular maps without normalizing/resolving.

statement (modern): The range pg≥2pa+4 has only the four listed types: ruled, χ=0 elliptic, genus-two products, and certain κ=1 surfaces with pa≥0.
gap or error (if any): The χ=0 type needs nontranslation monodromy; the historical proof of the general-type assertion was incomplete.
repair and reference: Beauville (1982), appendix to Debarre, pp. 343–346, proves the general-type inequality and equality case. For κ=1 use the canonical bundle formula (Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here)) and the finite-quotient/monodromy distinction of Catanese et al. notes: Source attributes the classification to Rosenblatt (1913) and Comessatti (1919,1922).

statement (modern): For a product of curves of genera two and g, pg=2g and pa=g−2.
repair and reference: Künneth: q=g+2, χ=g−1, K²=8(g−1).
notes: General type requires g≥2; g=1 belongs to κ=1.

statement (modern): A minimal general-type surface in this range is exactly such a product.
gap or error (if any): The source does not prove the cited classification; Beauville explicitly reports defects in the historical proofs.
repair and reference: Beauville (1982): χ≥(b−1)(g−1)≥q−3, combined with χ≤q−3; equality forces a product and min(b,g)=2.
notes: Documented modern repair, not a claim that the old proofs already establish it.

statement (modern): For minimal general type, P2−1=pa+p^(1)−1.
gap or error (if any): Requires pluricanonical vanishing, not RR alone.
repair and reference: P2=χ+K²; Xiao (1985), §1.1, and Part 1 plurigenus discussion.
notes: General formula Pm=χ+m(m−1)K²/2 for m≥2.

repair and reference: pa≥0 and p^(1)≥4 imply the bound.
notes: The numerical computation is correct.

statement (modern): A bicanonical system of this dimension gives a two-dimensional bicanonical image.
gap or error (if any): Dimension alone does not exclude a pencil; the source explicitly acknowledges the unresolved reducibility question.
repair and reference: Xiao (1985), Theorem 1 p.24: bicanonical map generically finite except pg=q=0,K²=1.
notes: The conclusion is correct in the stated range, but needs the later theorem.

statement (modern): The source permits a possibly multiple bicanonical projective presentation of the surface.
gap or error (if any): A multiple presentation is generically finite and may have degree greater than one; the wording does not assert a birational embedding.
repair and reference: Distinguish the image, covering degree, and canonical model. Chapter VIII supplies multiple canonical maps; Xiao (1985), Theorem 1, supplies the precise generically finite bicanonical conclusion.
notes: Do not attribute a stronger birationality claim to the phrase “magari multiplo”.

statement (modern): Surfaces with p^(1)=2 or 3 may all be regular apart from possible exceptions.
gap or error (if any): A proposal, not a proven theorem; p^(1)=3 has pg=q=1 examples.
repair and reference: Debarre (1982), Theorem 6.1, completed by the 1983 Addendum for the canonical-pencil case gives q=0 for K²=1. Lewis & Lyons (2018), Theorem 2.1, gives K²=2 irregular double covers of E^(2).
notes: The footnote’s Chapter IV §§18–20 should be Chapter VIII.

statement (modern): The final P12=0 row divides ruled surfaces by pa=0,−1,<−1.
gap or error (if any): Exceptional curves and transformation-family language carry the earlier qualifications.
repair and reference: Class A and corrected §8.
notes: Base genus is −pa in the irrational cases.

statement (modern): The final P12=1 row lists K3, abelian, Enriques and seven bielliptic types.
gap or error (if any): Polarized families are not individual surfaces; one repeated P4 should be P6.
repair and reference: The torsion table gives Pm=1 iff ord(K) divides m.
notes: The four zero-or-one plurigenera in the row are not independent choices.

statement (modern): For χ=0 and κ=1, the genus-one-fibration base has genus pg.
gap or error (if any): Incomplete: nontrivial Hodge character gives base genus pg+1.
repair and reference: Canonical bundle formula and Leray; Bombieri & Mumford (1977), §1, Theorem 2, pp. 27–29 (their L is the dual of the Hodge line used here); Catanese et al. (2025), Lemma 1.1; commentary XI §§4,7–8. Explicit counterexamples in Chapter X and XI §4.
notes: This error is present in the printed final table, not just the prose.

statement (modern): For χ>0 and κ=1, the base genus equals pg−pa.
repair and reference: Leray and positive degree of the Hodge line.
notes: Correct row.

statement (modern): For P12>1, the inequality n<2π−2 distinguishes the positive-canonical classes.
gap or error (if any): Must concern a sufficiently positive system; genus-one fibres have equality.
repair and reference: Adjunction with ample H and nontrivial nef K.
notes: The table’s compressed wording suppresses the choice of system.

statement (modern): If pg>3, a general-type surface has a canonical projective model.
gap or error (if any): Dimension of |K| alone does not exclude a pencil or establish birationality.
repair and reference: Require a generically finite/birational canonical map as appropriate; 5K is uniformly safe by Bombieri (1973).
notes: Canonical multiple-map and pencil distinctions from Chapter VIII must remain.

statement (modern): If p^(1)>3, the bicanonical image is a surface, perhaps covered multiply.
gap or error (if any): The source’s own pencil gap is inherited.
repair and reference: Xiao (1985), Theorem 1, resolves the gap.
notes: No universal bicanonical birationality is claimed by the repair.

statement (modern): For fixed p^(1)>1 there are finitely many general-type families.
gap or error (if any): Interpret as bounded algebraic families; not finite isomorphism classes. Source lacks the bounded embedding proof.
repair and reference: Noether gives 1≤χ≤(K²+6)/2; finitely many χ, then the 5K Hilbert polynomial gives finite type.
notes: Strengthens fixed (pa,pg,K²) boundedness by bounding the remaining χ values.
